what_its_for: Aripiprazole is used to treat several mental health conditions. These include schizophrenia (a condition that affects how you think and feel), bipolar disorder (extreme mood swings between highs and lows), major depression (when added to an antidepressant), irritability linked to autism, and Tourette's disorder (uncontrolled movements or sounds). It works by helping to balance certain natural chemicals in your brain called dopamine and serotonin.
how_to_take: Take aripiprazole by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If you are using the liquid form, use the measuring device that comes with your medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. If you have the tablet that dissolves in your mouth (orally disintegrating tablet), do not open the package until you are ready to take it. Peel back the foil carefully, place the tablet on your tongue, and let it dissolve. You do not need water. If you receive aripiprazole as a shot (injection), a healthcare provider will give it to you in a clinic or doctor's office — you will not give it to yourself at home.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. The dose depends on your age, weight, the condition being treated, and how well you respond to the medicine. Most adults start with 10 to 15 mg per day for conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine on your own without talking to your doctor first. Stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and you remember the same day, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed one and just take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are on the long-acting injection (Abilify Maintena or Aristada) and miss a scheduled appointment, call your doctor right away to reschedule.
storage: Store aripiprazole tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the liquid form in the refrigerator if instructed, and use it within 6 months of opening. Keep all medicines out of reach of children. Do not flush medicines down the toilet or pour them down the drain unless instructed. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking aripiprazole — it can increase dizziness, drowsiness, and other side effects. Be careful driving, operating machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially during hot weather or exercise, as aripiprazole can make it harder for your body to cool down. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some can interact with aripiprazole.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you notice: thoughts of hurting yourself or others (especially in children, teens, and young adults — risk may be higher in the first few weeks); uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (this could be a condition called tardive dyskinesia); very high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or fast heartbeat (signs of a rare but serious reaction called neuroleptic malignant syndrome); signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, hunger, or urination; feeling faint or lightheaded when you stand up quickly; chest pain or pounding heartbeat; or severe allergic reaction with rash, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you feel more depressed, very anxious, or have unusual urges (such as gambling, eating, shopping, or sexual urges) that are hard to control.
when_it_works: Aripiprazole does not work overnight. Most people begin to notice some improvement — such as better sleep or feeling less agitated — within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit of the medicine. It is important to keep taking it every day, even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults: Aripiprazole is not approved for use in older adults with dementia-related behavior problems and may increase the risk of serious side effects, including stroke and death. Talk to your doctor about risks and benefits. Children and teenagers: Aripiprazole can be used in children for certain conditions (such as irritability with autism, Tourette's, and schizophrenia in teens), but they should be closely watched for worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm, especially at the start of treatment. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Babies born to mothers who took this medicine in the third trimester may have withdrawal symptoms. Breastfeeding: Aripiprazole can pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about whether to breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if needed.
